sonnet.problem: The card says 'a new voice speaks: the Servant' and presents this as fact. Verses 4-9 only say 'Me', and 'His Servant' appears only in third person in verse 10. The speaker is named without the passage saying so.
sonnet.rule: When the text doesn't say who is speaking, he doesn't guess. He uses a plain lead-in, like "Then the psalm says…", and names a speaker only when the passage or its heading does.

sonnet.problem: The question's setup says the LORD 'turns rivers into a desert' before asking what His rebuke does to the sea. That strongly implies drying and rules out the wrong answers 'Splits it in two' and 'Calms its waves'.
sonnet.rule: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

sonnet.problem: The right answer 'Trust in the name of the LORD' is the verse's exact wording and sounds more like the Bible than the plain, modern-sounding wrong answers 'Wait until the morning comes' and 'Find his own way out', so it stands out. The question also asks the baker to complete a line that begins 'Let him…'.
sonnet.rule: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.
